reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource context, full CompartmentDefinition structure report, deterministic aggregate, R4/R6 StructureDefinition evidence, core CompartmentDefinition instances, R4 maturity map, and behavior reports for direct CompartmentDefinition hits. No OperationDefinition, SearchParameter, or HTTP behavior finding directly listed CompartmentDefinition; shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were treated as context only.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 FMM 1/trial-use weakens the presumption that every wire break must be preserved in the base specification. It does not eliminate concern for central required fields such as `resource.code` or runtime compartment-membership semantics used by access control and `$everything` behavior.

overall.oneLineConclusion: CompartmentDefinition keeps its identity and core shape; R6 creates targeted code/behavior migration work, not an unavoidable major resource migration.

reasoning.thesisMd: The actual R4-to-R6 migration shape is a mostly retained metadata resource with a few important local changes. The hard forward breaks are `resource.documentation` removal and the required `resource.code` binding moving to the R6 resource-type universe. The former is optional and rare; the latter is central but tied to the normal FHIR release resource inventory rather than a redesign of CompartmentDefinition itself.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The same resource exists in R6 and the core elements `url`, `name`, `code`, `resource.code`, and `resource.param` remain recognizable. R6 adds optional metadata (`title`, `versionAlgorithm[x]`) and optional `$everything` date-window mapping fields (`resource.startParam`, `resource.endParam`). The main forward migration task is version-aware handling of `resource.code` values whose resource types were removed, renamed, or replaced between releases; this is a targeted terminology/content migration, not a wholesale instance model remodel.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because no resource identity break or broad content-model replacement occurred, preventing individual avoidable breaks still has value. That said, compatibility preservation should be selective: indefinitely accepting obsolete resource-type codes in the R6 required binding would conflict with the R6 resource universe, while preserving or documenting optional legacy fields and alias behavior can reduce migration cost without changing the R6 model's goal.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The clearest low-cost preservation opportunity is `resource.documentation`: R6 could have retained the optional string as deprecated legacy prose or defined a standard extension for migration. For `resource.param`, the less-breaking path is not a different data shape but explicit transition guidance that servers normalize aliases to core HL7 SearchParameter codes. For `resource.code`, a base value-set widening is not clearly appropriate, but standard ConceptMaps or an extension carrying the original release code would reduce lossy migrations. The additive fields and warning constraints do not warrant base compatibility redesign.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: There are no direct behavior/API findings whose affected resources include CompartmentDefinition. The 11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings remain relevant to generic infrastructure clients, but they are not resource-level CompartmentDefinition changes and do not move the conclusion.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I broadly agree with the deterministic aggregate's `No` major migration, `mostly-stable-with-local-breaks` shape, and `preserve-compatibility-per-change` posture. The count-based summary is directionally right, but the substantive reason is that `resource.code` and `resource.param` are central targeted migration points while most other findings are additive, reverse-only, warning-level, or rare optional-field loss.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Real-world prevalence of custom CompartmentDefinition instances and server-specific `resource.param` alias use is not known from the reports. The R6 ballot package also appears internally inconsistent around compartment type codes, with a `Group` compartment instance observed while the inspected terminology evidence called out `EpisodeOfCare`.

findingConsiderations.title: CompartmentDefinition.resource.code required binding changed to the R6 resource-type universe
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the most material finding. `resource.code` is required on every resource row, and the R4/R6 required value sets differ substantially. R4 rows naming removed resource types become invalid in R6 and generated enums or compartment routing tables must be updated. This creates a real targeted migration step, but it follows the FHIR release resource inventory rather than proving a major CompartmentDefinition remodel.

findingConsiderations.title: CompartmentDefinition.resource.documentation was removed
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a direct old-valid/new-invalid wire break and was avoidable by retaining a deprecated optional string. Its practical weight is limited by FMM 1 and observed rarity in core instances, so it should be treated as a local migration chore or low-priority preservation opportunity rather than a resource-level migration driver.

findingConsiderations.title: resource.param now explicitly means the core HL7 SearchParameter code, not a server alias
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: No instance shape changes, but the runtime meaning is important because compartment membership can affect authorization and `$everything` behavior. The R6 clarification has a strong interoperability rationale, yet implementers relying on server-specific search-code aliases need explicit normalization and transition guidance.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds resource.startParam and resource.endParam for $everything date-window interpretation
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: These are optional additions and do not invalidate R4 instances. They matter for R6-to-R4 round trips or older tooling that consumes R6 definitions, but they are not a forward R4-to-R6 break and do not make a migration program unavoidable.

findingConsiderations.title: CompartmentDefinition.code required binding adds an R6 compartment type
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The binding expansion is forward-compatible for existing R4 compartment codes, so it does not drive the migration conclusion. The observed R6 package inconsistency around `Group` versus the inspected compartment-type terminology should still be resolved before implementers finalize generated enums or validation policy.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds top-level title and versionAlgorithm[x] metadata
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Optional metadata additions are forward-compatible. They may need extension or sidecar handling for R6-to-R4 fidelity, but they are not a reason to treat R4-to-R6 migration as major.

findingConsiderations.title: Warning-level canonical constraints were added or tightened for name and url
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The constraints are warning-level hygiene checks. Warning-as-error pipelines may need suppression or data cleanup updates, but ordinary R6 structural validity is preserved.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding can affect generic infrastructure clients, but CompartmentDefinition is neither Resource nor DomainResource for purposes of this resource-level review. It is context, not a CompartmentDefinition-specific migration driver.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Define a version-aware `resource.code` migration policy: map renamed/replaced resource types, intentionally drop rows for resources removed from R6, and preserve original R4 codes in an extension or audit trail when the mapping is lossy.

Update compartment-membership runtime logic to treat `resource.param` as the core HL7 SearchParameter code and add tests for server-specific alias normalization, especially for authorization and `$everything` use cases.
Decide whether populated R4 `resource.documentation` should be dropped, moved to an extension, or preserved out of band; this is a low-cost compatibility choice but not a major migration blocker.
Review the R6 compartment-type terminology and core CompartmentDefinition instances for the observed `Group`/`EpisodeOfCare` inconsistency before locking generated enums.

caveats: No direct behavior/API finding affected CompartmentDefinition; shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were considered only as context.
FMM 1/trial-use status means compatibility pressure is weak, and the reports do not prove broad production use of custom CompartmentDefinition instances.
The conclusion could change if downstream evidence shows heavy production reliance on local CompartmentDefinition artifacts with removed resource types or server-specific search parameter aliases.
